To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extinction probability in a continuous-time multi-type branching process in a periodic environment equals (resp. is less than) 1 when the basic reproduction number is less than (bigger than)  1.

for a certain class of periodic multi-type branching processes the extinction probability can be calculated from the basic reproduction number and that for the linear SEIR epidemic model with periodic transmission rates and periodic vaccination rates the basic reproduction number can be calculated from data on incidence and vaccination rates.

for a certain class of continuous-time and discrete-time multi-type branching processes with periodic environment, the extinction probability can be computed explicitly in terms of the basic reproduction number.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how to use the theory of differential equations to study the asymptotic behavior and the probability of extinction of a population in a periodic environment?
the following question: how can one measure the epidemic risk of an infectious disease in a periodic environment?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the probability of extinction of a population in a periodic environment is equal to 1 if the average of the basic reproduction number is less than 1.

the probability of extinction is a good indicator of the epidemic risk, but it is not the only one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the extinction probability in a periodic environment may be computed by a simple formula involving the basic reproduction number and the asymptotic behavior in a periodic environment of a system of differential equations with the same structure as the model.
the extinction probability in a periodic environment may be calculated using the extinction probability in the corresponding constant environment.
we have shown how to use results from the theory of periodic cooperative systems in the context of branching processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probability of extinction is a useful indicator of epidemic risks and can be used to assess the impact of vaccination campaigns.

the probability of extinction of a population is related to the basic reproduction number in a very similar manner as the probability that the population size goes extinct in discrete-time branching processes is related to the mean offspring number.
the probability of extinction can be used as a tool to assess the epidemic risk in a time-periodic environment.
